questions.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with a thyroid condition?
questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; ATA thyroid guidelines 2021

questions.text: Do you feel unusually cold when others are comfortable, or have a persistent low body temperature?
questions.source: Garber et al. AACE/ATA hypothyroidism guidelines 2012; OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: Have you noticed significant hair thinning or hair loss (not male-pattern baldness)?
questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; Blume-Peytavi et al. JDDG 2011

questions.text: Have you had unexplained weight gain or weight loss (≥5 kg in 3 months, without intentional diet change)?
questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; Braverman & Cooper Thyroid 2012

questions.text: Do you experience heat intolerance, heart palpitations, or tremors at rest?
questions.source: Ross et al. ATA hyperthyroidism guidelines 2016

questions.text: Over the past month, how often have you felt that your stress was uncontrollable or overwhelming?
questions.source: Cohen PSS-4 1983; McEwen allostatic load framework 1998

questions.text: Do you regularly work night shifts, rotating shifts, or have severely irregular sleep–wake times?
questions.source: Vetter et al. JCEM 2015; Schernhammer circadian disruption meta-analysis

questions.text: Have you experienced spontaneous breast milk production (galactorrhoea), breast tenderness (outside pregnancy), or been told you have high prolactin?
questions.source: Melmed et al. Endocr Rev 2011; OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: On average, how much direct sunlight (face and arms uncovered) do you get per day?

responses.label: < 15 min/day or fully covered / indoor worker

questions.source: Holick vitamin D deficiency review NEJM 2007; OMICS Introductory Report

questions.text: Do you regularly take vitamin D supplements?

responses.label: Yes — daily ≥800 IU or prescribed dose

questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; Pludowski et al. Nutrients 2022

questions.text: Have you had a fragility fracture (from a low-energy fall or minor trauma) or been diagnosed with osteoporosis / osteopenia?
questions.source: Kanis et al. Osteoporos Int FRAX methodology 2008

questions.text: Are you currently trying to conceive (or attempting to start a pregnancy in the next 12 months)?

responses.label: Yes — >12 months without success (or known fertility treatment)

questions.source: WHO infertility definition; NICE fertility guidelines 2023

questions.text: How regular are your menstrual cycles?

responses.label: Infrequent / long cycles (>35 days) or fewer than 9/year
Absent (no period for ≥3 months, not pregnant or menopausal)

triggers.if_response: Infrequent / long cycles (>35 days) or fewer than 9/year
Absent (no period for ≥3 months, not pregnant or menopausal)

questions.source: Rotterdam PCOS criteria 2003; FIGO menstrual disorders classification 2018

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)?
questions.source: Rotterdam PCOS criteria 2003; Teede et al. Int J Gynaecol Obstet 2023 PCOS guideline

questions.text: Do you experience hirsutism (excess facial / body hair) or persistent acne related to hormones?

responses.label: Mild — some facial hair or occasional acne
Moderate-to-severe hirsutism or persistent hormonal acne

questions.source: Azziz et al. excess androgen criteria; Rotterdam PCOS 2003

questions.text: Do you experience hot flushes / flashes or night sweats?

responses.label: Moderate — several per day / disrupting sleep

questions.source: Menopause Society (NAMS) 2023 position statement; Greene Climacteric Scale

questions.text: What is your current menopause status?
questions.source: STRAW+10 staging criteria; NAMS 2023

questions.text: Have you noticed a significant decrease in sexual desire or libido over the past 3 months?

responses.label: Significant decrease — affects relationship or wellbeing

questions.source: NAMS female sexual dysfunction position statement 2019

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with or told you have low testosterone (hypogonadism)?
questions.source: Bhasin et al. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2018 testosterone guideline; EAU andrology guidelines

questions.text: How often do you experience morning erections (nocturnal penile tumescence)?
questions.source: Buvat et al. J Sex Med 2010; Araujo & McKinlay testosterone deficiency review

questions.text: Over the past 4 weeks, how would you rate your sex drive and overall energy level?

responses.label: Very low — markedly affecting quality of life

questions.source: ADAM questionnaire (Morley et al.); AMS andropause scale

questions.text: Have you experienced a combination of reduced muscle mass, increased body fat (especially belly), low mood, or reduced stamina over the past year?
questions.source: Heinemann AMS scale; Buvat et al. late-onset hypogonadism ISSAM guidelines

questions.text: Has a semen analysis or fertility workup revealed any abnormality (e.g. low count, poor motility)?

responses.label: Mild abnormality (e.g. borderline count or motility)

questions.source: WHO semen analysis reference values 2021; Tournaye et al. EAU male infertility

questions.text: Do you experience any of the following? (select all that apply): persistent sugar cravings, afternoon energy crashes, skin tags, dark patches of skin (acanthosis nigricans), or being told you are pre-diabetic.
questions.source: OMICS Introductory Report; Fauser et al. PCOS metabolic phenotype; ADA prediabetes criteria

questions.text: Which best describes your typical daily energy and alertness pattern?

responses.label: Alert in morning, stable through day, good sleep
Sluggish morning but improves — afternoon dip is manageable
Wired at night but exhausted in morning (reversed rhythm)
Flat / exhausted all day regardless of sleep

questions.source: Clow et al. cortisol awakening response review; Tsigos & Chrousos HPA axis review

questions.text: Are you taking or have you taken long-term corticosteroids (prednisone, dexamethasone, or inhaled steroids for >3 months)?

responses.label: Short course only (<3 months, now stopped)
Current or long-term oral corticosteroids (>3 months)

questions.source: Fardet & Petri glucocorticoid iatrogenic effects review JAMA IM 2019

questions.text: Which of the following apply to you? (select all): dark skin tone, strict vegan / avoid dairy, BMI > 30, kidney disease, or living above 35° latitude with limited outdoor time in winter.
questions.source: Holick NEJM 2007; SACN vitamin D report 2016

questions.text: Which of the following apply to you? (select all): low calcium intake, lack of weight-bearing exercise, long-term proton-pump inhibitor (PPI) or anticonvulsant use, heavy smoking, or early menopause.

responses.label: Low calcium intake (rare dairy, fortified foods, or supplements)
Long-term PPI or anticonvulsant use (>1 year)

questions.source: Kanis FRAX model; IOF osteoporosis clinical risk factors 2019

questions.text: Have you or your partner been diagnosed with a cause of female-factor subfertility (e.g. blocked tubes, endometriosis, uterine abnormality)?
questions.source: NICE fertility guideline NG156 2023; Toftager et al. subfertility predictors

questions.text: How long does it typically take you to recover after moderate physical exertion (e.g. a brisk 30-minute walk)?

responses.label: I feel fine during and after — normal recovery
Unusually exhausted for hours / rest of the day
Exercise intolerant — I avoid it because of how bad I feel afterwards

questions.source: WHO-5 wellbeing index; Nater & Rohleder salivary cortisol fatigue studies
